newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees no quick peace in PNG.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees no quick peace in PNG.

text.p: Australia said on Friday it did not expect a quick end to a secessionist war in neighbouring Papua New Guinea, despite a fresh peace initiative by Port Moresby.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer welcomed Papua New Guinea's announcement that it would seek a negotiated settlement with rebels fighting for independence for Bougainville island, instead of trying to end the war with military force.
But he said the decision would not bring immediate peace.
"Frankly, the process of peace in Bougainville is going to have to take a great deal of patience -- I don't think we can expect instant breakthroughs overnight," Downer said in a radio interview.

Papua New Guinea caretaker Prime Minister John Giheno announced the peace plan on Thursday and said the government in Port Moresby, rocked by an army rebellion two months ago against plans to use mercenaries to end the war, now believed there could be no military solution.
"Rather, the main objective of the strategy is stated as to find a peaceful and lasting resolution of the Bougainville conflict, without reliance on military force," Giheno said
Giheno said the plan was developed under the direction of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, in a process which began before Chan was forced to stand aside in March by an army mutiny.

The strategy includes negotiations with the rebel Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA), increased control of their own affairs by Bougainvilleans and a move towards peacekeeping operations for the Papua New Guinea military on the resource-rich island, 800 kilometres (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby.
The island is the site of the vast Panguna copper-gold mine, controlled by Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
Chan and two senior ministers were forced by the army mutiny and civilian protests to stand aside in March, pending completion of an official inquiry into the mercenary contract.

Many past rounds of peace talks between Port Moresby and the rebel army and military offensives have failed to resolve the conflict, which closed the rich Panguna copper mine and killed thousands of people.
